slides.headline: She is listening to her lover. Look at the doorway.
slides.sub: Edmund Blair Leighton, The End of the Song, 1902

slides.headline: The legend
slides.text: In the legend, the knight Tristan falls in love with Isolde, who is married to his own uncle, King Mark.

slides.headline: The song
slides.text: Here, in a quiet garden, Tristan plays the harp and sings to her. It is their secret moment, far from the court.

slides.headline: Isolde
slides.text: She leans back, eyes half closed, lost in the music and in him. For a moment she forgets she is a queen.

slides.headline: Tristan
slides.text: He leans in close, almost touching her face, his harp between them like the only thing keeping them apart.

slides.headline: The doorway
slides.text: But look on the right. Half hidden in the shadows, King Mark has stepped in. He has heard everything.

slides.headline: The title
slides.text: The painting is called The End of the Song. The music has stopped, and so has their secret.

slides.headline: The story
slides.text: The tale of Tristan and Isolde inspired poems, Wagner's opera and countless paintings. It rarely ends well for the lovers.

slides.headline: Your choice
slides.text: Loyalty to the king, or love for the queen? If you were Tristan, which would you choose right now?
